pr.title: Name the head GitHub shows after review ready or hold moves the draft state
pr.head: af22d1f29a0b90a25c0c4d21a94ecc92f4a116fc

summary: project review ready marks the author's own draft pull request ready for review, and project review hold converts it back to a draft. Agents run them around a push: fix-pr holds a signed-off pull request, pushes a change, and then marks it ready. Each command prints one line naming the pull request's head, such as marked acme/app#1 ready for review at 4f2a9c1, so the reader knows which commit now waits for review.

Both commands read the pull request from GitHub, run gh pr ready, and read the pull request back to confirm that the draft state moved. They took the head from the first read. Right after a push, GitHub can still show the previous head for a few seconds, so the line could name a commit that was no longer the pull request's head.

The change takes the head from the read-back instead, which runs later and sees a recent push more often. When the read-back has no head, the command falls back to the first read. A pull request already in the requested state makes only one read, so it reports that read's head. The documentation now says which head the line names and that it can still trail a push made a moment before.

groups.title: Report the head from the read-back
groups.kicker: set_draft names the head GitHub shows after the draft state moves
intro: set_draft in src/projector/review.py is the shared body of review ready and review hold. It refuses a pull request that is closed or that someone else wrote, runs gh pr ready (with --undo for hold), and reads the pull request back from GitHub's REST API to confirm the draft state.

The change keeps that read-back in a variable, after, and uses its head in the result when it has one. The documentation in docs/cli.md describes the new rule and its limit, and a test in tests/test_review.py has the fake GitHub move the head while gh pr ready runs.

checks.text: review_draft in src/projector/cli.py is the only caller of set_draft. It prints the result as one line or as JSON, and no skill or daemon reads the head field to decide anything. Checked by searching the repository.

files.note: The read-back after gh pr ready now supplies the head that the command prints.

checks.text: The fallback to the first read applies only when the read-back returns no head. GitHub's REST API always includes one for a pull request, so in practice the read-back's head is the one printed.

files.note: Adds an after_ready hook to the fake GitHub and a test that moves the head while gh pr ready runs.

checks.text: The new test fails when the fix is reverted: it expects fffffff and gets the earlier head. Checked by reverting the line in a copy of the source and running DraftTests.

files.note: Says the line names the head GitHub shows once the state has moved, and, after the example, that it can trail a push made a moment before.

checks.text: The note about GitHub's lag follows the example output, so the sample reads as the ordinary case rather than as a stale head. The second commit moved it there, as the first review suggested.
